majorInteractions: CNS depressants can increase sedation. Psychostimulants and MAOIs can increase the risk of elevated blood pressure.
monitoring: Administer under medical supervision. Check blood pressure before and after dosing, monitor respiration and sedation for at least two hours, and assess stability before discharge.

eliminationHalfLife.basis: Terminal elimination range after nasal administration

doseUseReferences.scheduleText: Intranasally twice weekly for the first four weeks under supervision in a healthcare setting

substances.name: Lithium Carbonate
substances.summary: Oral lithium carbonate capsules. Dosing is expressed as lithium carbonate mass, while monitoring measures serum lithium ion concentration.

indications: The US label covers acute manic or mixed episodes and maintenance treatment of bipolar I disorder.
contraindications: Hypersensitivity to capsule excipients. Avoid use in severe renal impairment per the cited label.
majorWarnings: Therapeutic and toxic concentrations are close. Dehydration, changes in sodium balance and reduced renal function can increase toxicity. Long-term therapy also warrants renal and thyroid monitoring.
majorInteractions: Diuretics, NSAIDs and renin–angiotensin system antagonists can raise serum lithium.
monitoring: Check renal function, electrolytes and thyroid function at baseline. Obtain serum lithium around 12 hours after the last oral dose per label and follow renal and thyroid function.

doseUseReferences.indication: Manic or mixed episodes of bipolar I disorder
doseUseReferences.population: Adults without a renal dose adjustment
doseUseReferences.amountText: Initially 300 mg lithium carbonate per dose
doseUseReferences.scheduleText: Orally three times daily, adjusted according to serum lithium and response

substances.name: Valproate
substances.summary: The cited solution contains sodium valproate with strength expressed as valproic acid equivalent.

indications: Labeled partial, absence and selected other seizures.
contraindications: Significant hepatic disease, specified POLG-related mitochondrial disease, urea-cycle disorders or related hypersensitivity.
majorWarnings: Risks include hepatotoxicity, pancreatitis, fetal harm, hyperammonemia and thrombocytopenia.
majorInteractions: Can raise lamotrigine exposure. Carbapenems can lower valproate concentrations.
monitoring: Monitor hepatic function, blood counts and response, measuring drug or ammonia levels when indicated.

doseUseReferences.population: Adults and patients aged ten or older
doseUseReferences.amountText: Initial 10–15 mg/kg/day, as valproic acid equivalent
doseUseReferences.scheduleText: Orally in divided doses above 250 mg/day, titrating per label

substances.name: Divalproex
substances.summary: The cited US extended-release tablets contain divalproex sodium, with strength expressed as valproic acid equivalent.

drugClass: Valproate antiseizure medicine and mood stabilizer
indications: Used for manic or mixed episodes, selected seizures and migraine prevention.
contraindications: Hepatic disease or significant dysfunction, specified POLG-related mitochondrial disorders, urea-cycle disorders or hypersensitivity. For migraine prevention, contraindicated during pregnancy or in women of childbearing potential without effective contraception.
majorWarnings: Risks include severe hepatic injury, pancreatitis and fetal harm. Thrombocytopenia and hyperammonemia may also occur.
majorInteractions: Can increase lamotrigine exposure. Carbapenems can substantially reduce valproate concentrations.
monitoring: Check hepatic function at baseline and early in treatment. Follow blood counts and coagulation, measure concentrations when indicated, and consider ammonia testing with altered mental status.

eliminationHalfLife.basis: Range of mean terminal half-lives during oral valproate monotherapy

doseUseReferences.amountText: 500 mg per day for the first week, expressed as valproic acid
doseUseReferences.scheduleText: Extended-release tablet orally once daily, with later titration per label

substances.name: Carbamazepine
substances.summary: The cited product is a standard carbamazepine tablet. Repeated use can induce its own metabolism.

indications: The cited US label covers selected seizure types and trigeminal neuralgia.
contraindications: History of marrow suppression, hypersensitivity to carbamazepine or related tricyclic compounds, and concomitant nefazodone. The label calls for at least 14 days after stopping MAOIs.
majorWarnings: Severe skin reactions, marrow suppression, hepatic injury and hyponatremia may occur. Evaluate HLA-B*15:02 in genetically at-risk populations.
majorInteractions: Enzyme induction can reduce exposure to many drugs and some hormonal contraceptives. Certain CYP3A4 inhibitors can raise carbamazepine levels.
monitoring: Follow blood counts, hepatic function and sodium as appropriate. Consider plasma levels when indicated.

eliminationHalfLife.basis: With repeated dosing, compared with about 25–65 hours initially

doseUseReferences.amountText: Standard tablets initially 200 mg per dose
doseUseReferences.scheduleText: Orally twice daily, then adjusted to seizure control and tolerance

substances.name: Oxcarbazepine
substances.summary: The cited product is an oral suspension, with activity largely mediated by the monohydroxy metabolite MHD.

indications: Partial-onset seizures, with age limits differing for monotherapy and adjunctive use.
contraindications: Hypersensitivity to oxcarbazepine, ingredients or eslicarbazepine acetate.
majorWarnings: Hyponatremia, serious rash, DRESS, dizziness and unsteadiness may occur.
majorInteractions: Can reduce some hormonal contraceptive exposures. Carbamazepine and certain other drugs can reduce MHD concentrations.
monitoring: Follow sodium, seizures, rash and neurological effects, and check dosing against renal function.

eliminationHalfLife.basis: Active MHD metabolite, versus about two hours for the parent drug

doseUseReferences.scheduleText: Oral suspension in two divided doses

substances.name: Lamotrigine
substances.summary: The cited product is a lamotrigine orally disintegrating tablet. Starting and titration schedules depend on concomitant medicines.

indications: Used for selected seizure indications and bipolar I maintenance as specified in the cited label.
contraindications: Prior hypersensitivity to lamotrigine or formulation ingredients.
majorWarnings: Life-threatening rashes can occur. Risk can rise with valproate, an excessive starting dose or overly rapid titration.
majorInteractions: Valproate slows clearance. Some antiseizure medicines and estrogen-containing contraceptives can reduce lamotrigine exposure.
monitoring: Follow rash, fever, mucosal symptoms, response and tolerability. Recheck the label titration schedule before restarting after interruption.

eliminationHalfLife.basis: Mean after repeated dosing in healthy volunteers taking no other medicines

doseUseReferences.population: Adults taking neither valproate nor the listed inducers
doseUseReferences.amountText: 25 mg per day in weeks one and two
doseUseReferences.scheduleText: Orally once daily, with gradual titration per label and interacting medicines

substances.name: Hydroxyzine
substances.summary: The cited UK film-coated tablets contain hydroxyzine hydrochloride and can cause sedation.

indications: Helps manage anxiety in adults and pruritus associated with urticaria or selected forms of dermatitis.
contraindications: Contraindications include ingredient hypersensitivity, known QT prolongation or specified risk factors for arrhythmia.
majorWarnings: Somnolence, anticholinergic adverse effects, QT prolongation and torsades de pointes may occur.
majorInteractions: Coadministration with medicines known to prolong QT or cause torsades is contraindicated. Alcohol and sedatives can intensify CNS depression.
monitoring: Assess arrhythmia risk and concomitant medicines, and follow sedation, response, palpitations or syncope.

eliminationHalfLife.basis: Approximate mean terminal elimination in the comparison subjects cited by the label

doseUseReferences.population: Adults, with separate assessment in older patients or hepatic or renal impairment
doseUseReferences.scheduleText: Orally at night, adjusted to need and tolerability

substances.name: Nitrazepam
substances.summary: The cited product is an oral nitrazepam tablet. Sedation may persist the next day.

indications: Short-term treatment of severe insomnia when daytime sedation is acceptable.
contraindications: Contraindications include hypersensitivity, severe respiratory or hepatic insufficiency, myasthenia gravis, sleep apnea and childhood.
majorWarnings: Somnolence, amnesia, falls, dependence and withdrawal may occur.
majorInteractions: Opioids, alcohol and other CNS depressants increase sedation and respiratory risk.
monitoring: Follow sleep, next-day alertness, breathing and dependence risk, and arrange gradual withdrawal.

doseUseReferences.population: Adults, with dose reduction for older or debilitated patients
doseUseReferences.scheduleText: Orally before bed

substances.name: Estazolam
substances.summary: Oral benzodiazepine with sedative effects.

indications: Short-term treatment of insomnia with difficulty initiating sleep, frequent nighttime awakening or early awakening.
contraindications: Hypersensitivity to this drug or benzodiazepines, or concomitant ketoconazole or itraconazole.
majorWarnings: Somnolence, impaired coordination, dependence and withdrawal may occur. Abrupt cessation can trigger severe withdrawal.
majorInteractions: Opioids, alcohol and other CNS depressants increase the risk of severe sedation and respiratory depression.
monitoring: Follow sleep, daytime alertness, breathing and dependence risk, and reassess persistent insomnia.

eliminationHalfLife.basis: Elimination range reported in the label

doseUseReferences.scheduleText: Orally at bedtime

substances.name: Lormetazepam
substances.summary: These details concern lormetazepam oral tablets.

indications: Short-term treatment of disabling or markedly distressing insomnia.
contraindications: Severe respiratory insufficiency, sleep apnea, myasthenia gravis, severe hepatic failure or hypersensitivity to benzodiazepines or ingredients.
majorWarnings: Somnolence, ataxia, falls, dependence and withdrawal can occur.
majorInteractions: Alcohol, opioids and other CNS depressants can intensify sedation and respiratory depression.
monitoring: Follow sleep, next-day alertness and breathing, assess falls and dependence risk, and agree on a discontinuation plan before initiation.

eliminationHalfLife.basis: Approximate terminal-phase value after oral dosing

doseUseReferences.population: Adults, with lower dosing preferred for older patients
doseUseReferences.scheduleText: Orally before bed

substances.name: Flurazepam
substances.summary: The cited oral capsules contain flurazepam hydrochloride. An active metabolite persists for a prolonged period.

indications: Used for insomnia with difficulty initiating sleep, frequent nighttime waking or early awakening.
contraindications: Hypersensitivity to flurazepam or other benzodiazepines.
majorWarnings: Next-day somnolence, unsteadiness and falls may occur. Repeated use can lead to accumulation, dependence and withdrawal.
majorInteractions: Opioids, alcohol and other CNS depressants can intensify sedation and respiratory depression.
monitoring: Follow sleep, next-day alertness, falls, breathing and dependence risk, particularly in older patients.

eliminationHalfLife.basis: Elimination range of the active metabolite N1-desalkylflurazepam

doseUseReferences.scheduleText: Orally before bed

substances.name: Clorazepate
substances.summary: The oral dipotassium salt is rapidly converted to the active metabolite nordiazepam.

indications: Used for anxiety disorders or short-term anxiety relief, adjunctive treatment of focal seizures, and acute alcohol withdrawal.
contraindications: Product hypersensitivity or acute narrow-angle glaucoma.
majorWarnings: Sedation, impaired coordination and dependence may occur. Rapid reduction or abrupt cessation can cause withdrawal and seizures.
majorInteractions: Opioids, alcohol and other CNS depressants can intensify sedation and respiratory depression.
monitoring: Reassess response, sedation, respiratory and dependence risks. Consider blood counts and hepatic tests during prolonged treatment as described in the label.

eliminationHalfLife.basis: Apparent plasma elimination of the active metabolite nordiazepam

doseUseReferences.amountText: Cited starting amount of 7.5–15 mg dipotassium salt per day
doseUseReferences.scheduleText: Orally, adjusted according to response and tolerability

substances.name: Prazepam
substances.summary: Long-acting anxiolytic with accumulation of active metabolites after repeated dosing.

indications: Short-term treatment of severe anxiety.
contraindications: Benzodiazepine hypersensitivity, myasthenia gravis, severe respiratory or hepatic insufficiency, or sleep apnea.
majorWarnings: Watch for sedation, falls, respiratory depression, dependence and withdrawal.
majorInteractions: Alcohol, opioids and other CNS depressants increase sedation and respiratory risk.
monitoring: Reassess anxiety, alertness and continued need, and taper gradually.

eliminationHalfLife.basis: Mean for major active metabolite norprazepam after repeated dosing

doseUseReferences.scheduleText: Orally once daily or in divided doses, individualized to response

substances.name: Clobazam
substances.summary: The cited US oral suspension contains clobazam as its sole active ingredient.

indications: Adjunctive therapy for seizures associated with Lennox–Gastaut syndrome in patients aged two years and older.
contraindications: Prior hypersensitivity to clobazam or formulation ingredients.
majorWarnings: Somnolence, dependence and withdrawal may occur. Serious cutaneous reactions include SJS/TEN and DRESS.
majorInteractions: Opioids or other CNS depressants can add sedation and respiratory depression. CYP2C19 inhibitors may increase active-metabolite exposure.
monitoring: Follow seizures, sedation, breathing, rash and hypersensitivity symptoms. Account for accumulation when adjusting dose.

eliminationHalfLife.basis: Parent-drug mean range, versus about 71–82 hours for the active metabolite

doseUseReferences.population: Age two years or older and weight up to 30 kg, with separate considerations for special populations
doseUseReferences.scheduleText: Oral suspension once daily, with titration per the label

substances.name: Tofisopam
substances.summary: The cited product is tofisopam 50 mg oral tablets.

indications: Psychological or somatic conditions with tension, anxiety or autonomic symptoms, and autonomic symptoms of alcohol withdrawal.
contraindications: Related hypersensitivity, decompensated respiratory insufficiency, sleep-apnea or coma history, or concomitant tacrolimus, sirolimus or cyclosporine.
majorWarnings: Agitation, insomnia, gastrointestinal symptoms or respiratory depression may occur. Seizures can be provoked in epilepsy.
majorInteractions: The listed immunosuppressants are contraindicated. Opioids and other CNS depressants add respiratory risk.
monitoring: Follow anxiety, agitation and breathing, checking hepatic or renal status and concurrent medicines.

doseUseReferences.scheduleText: Orally one to three times daily, individualized to response

substances.name: Zaleplon
substances.summary: The cited product is zaleplon oral capsules.

indications: Short-term insomnia treatment, studied primarily for sleep onset.
contraindications: Prior drug-related complex sleep behavior or related hypersensitivity.
majorWarnings: Somnolence, abnormal sleep behaviors, dependence and withdrawal may occur.
majorInteractions: Alcohol and other CNS depressants increase sedation and respiratory risk.
monitoring: Follow sleep and abnormal behavior, reassessing persistent insomnia.

doseUseReferences.population: Adults, with lower dosing for older patients or hepatic impairment
doseUseReferences.scheduleText: One oral dose immediately before bed

substances.name: Ramelteon
substances.summary: The cited product is a standard ramelteon oral tablet.

indications: Insomnia characterized by difficulty initiating sleep.
contraindications: Prior treatment-associated angioedema or concomitant fluvoxamine.
majorWarnings: Watch for somnolence, abnormal sleep behavior, hypersensitivity and mood changes.
majorInteractions: Fluvoxamine substantially raises exposure. Avoid alcohol and check other CYP inhibitors.
monitoring: Reassess sleep and next-day alertness. Avoid in severe hepatic impairment.

eliminationHalfLife.basis: Parent-drug range, with a longer-lived active metabolite

doseUseReferences.scheduleText: Orally within 30 minutes before bed, avoiding a high-fat meal

substances.name: Suvorexant
substances.summary: Oral hypnotic.

indications: Difficulty initiating or maintaining sleep.
contraindications: Narcolepsy.
majorWarnings: Impaired next-day alertness, complex sleep behaviors and sleep paralysis may occur.
majorInteractions: Strong CYP3A inhibitors raise exposure. Alcohol and CNS depressants add sedation.
monitoring: Follow sleep, daytime somnolence, abnormal behavior and mood.

doseUseReferences.scheduleText: At most once nightly within 30 minutes before bed, allowing at least seven hours before awakening

substances.name: Lemborexant
substances.summary: Oral hypnotic that suppresses wake-promoting signaling.

indications: Used in adults with difficulty initiating or maintaining sleep.
contraindications: Narcolepsy.
majorWarnings: May impair next-day alertness. Sleep paralysis, complex sleep behaviors or worsening depression may occur.
majorInteractions: Avoid moderate or strong CYP3A inhibitors or inducers. Alcohol and other CNS depressants can add sedation.
monitoring: Follow sleep, next-day sleepiness, abnormal sleep behaviors and mood.

eliminationHalfLife.basis: Effective half-life, 17 hours at 5 mg and 19 hours at 10 mg

doseUseReferences.population: Adults, with separate checks for hepatic impairment or interactions
doseUseReferences.scheduleText: Orally once immediately before bed, with at least seven hours before planned awakening

substances.name: Daridorexant
substances.summary: Oral hypnotic that suppresses wake-promoting signaling.

indications: Adult insomnia involving difficulty initiating or maintaining sleep.
contraindications: Narcolepsy or hypersensitivity to daridorexant or formulation ingredients.
majorWarnings: May impair next-day alertness. Sleep paralysis, complex sleep behaviors or worsening depression can occur.
majorInteractions: Avoid strong CYP3A4 inhibitors and moderate or strong CYP3A4 inducers. Alcohol and CNS depressants can add sedation.
monitoring: Follow sleep response, daytime sleepiness and abnormal sleep behaviors. Assess risk in respiratory impairment.

doseUseReferences.population: Adults, with separate hepatic and interaction considerations
doseUseReferences.scheduleText: One oral dose within 30 minutes before bedtime, with at least seven hours before planned awakening

substances.name: Brotizolam
substances.summary: The cited Dutch tablets contain 0.25 mg each.

indications: Short-term treatment of severe, impairing insomnia.
contraindications: Hypersensitivity, myasthenia gravis, severe respiratory depression, sleep apnea, severe hepatic impairment and age under 18 years.
majorWarnings: Sedation, impaired memory, dependence and withdrawal can occur.
majorInteractions: Alcohol, opioids and other CNS depressants can worsen sedation or respiratory depression. CYP3A4 inhibitors may alter exposure.
monitoring: Reassess sleep, next-day alertness and respiratory risk. The label generally limits treatment to two weeks.

tmax.basis: Mean about 45 minutes after swallowing 0.25 mg

doseUseReferences.population: Adults, with a lower starting dose for older patients
doseUseReferences.scheduleText: One oral dose on an empty stomach immediately before bed

substances.name: Quazepam
substances.summary: Oral hypnotic with long-lived active metabolites.

indications: Insomnia involving sleep initiation, frequent awakenings or early awakening.
contraindications: Hypersensitivity to quazepam or benzodiazepines.
majorWarnings: Watch for next-day sedation, falls, dependence and withdrawal.
majorInteractions: Opioids, alcohol and other CNS depressants add severe sedation and respiratory risk.
monitoring: Reassess sleep, alertness, breathing and dependence, and taper on withdrawal.

eliminationHalfLife.basis: Parent-drug mean, with a longer-lived active metabolite

doseUseReferences.scheduleText: Orally before bed

substances.name: Loprazolam
substances.summary: The cited product is a 1 mg oral tablet.

indications: Short-term treatment of severe insomnia, including difficulty falling asleep or frequent awakenings.
contraindications: Benzodiazepine hypersensitivity, acute pulmonary or severe respiratory insufficiency, myasthenia gravis, sleep apnea and specified psychiatric contexts.
majorWarnings: Somnolence, amnesia, falls, dependence and withdrawal may occur.
majorInteractions: Alcohol, opioids and other CNS depressants can add sedation or respiratory depression.
monitoring: Follow sleep, next-day alertness, breathing and dependence risk, and agree on a discontinuation plan.

eliminationHalfLife.basis: Mean in five subjects after one 1 mg dose, measured by HPLC/GC

doseUseReferences.population: Adults, with lower initiation for frail patients
doseUseReferences.scheduleText: Orally at bedtime

substances.name: Chloral Hydrate
substances.summary: The cited UK product is a 143 mg/5 mL oral solution.

indications: Short-term treatment of severe insomnia impairing daily life after other options fail. Pediatric use is restricted to eligible patients with neurodevelopmental disorders under specialist care.
contraindications: Hypersensitivity, severe hepatic, renal or cardiac disease, active gastritis or esophagitis, gastroduodenal ulceration or perforation, and susceptibility to acute porphyria.
majorWarnings: Watch for excessive sedation, respiratory depression, arrhythmias and dependence. The cited course is limited to two weeks.
majorInteractions: Alcohol and other CNS depressants can intensify sedation. Check for other QT-prolonging medicines.
monitoring: Assess alertness, breathing and cardiac risk. Repeat courses require specialist reassessment.

eliminationHalfLife.basis: Plasma elimination of trichloroethanol, the active metabolite

doseUseReferences.scheduleText: One oral dose of the 143 mg/5 mL solution 15–30 minutes before bedtime

substances.name: Clomethiazole
substances.summary: The cited soft capsules contain 192 mg clomethiazole base each.

indications: Used for restlessness or agitation in older patients, short-term treatment of severe insomnia in older patients, and closely supervised treatment of alcohol withdrawal.
contraindications: Hypersensitivity to ingredients or acute pulmonary insufficiency.
majorWarnings: Respiratory depression, excessive sedation and dependence may occur. Exposure may increase in older adults or in hepatic impairment.
majorInteractions: Alcohol and other CNS depressants can substantially increase depressant effects.
monitoring: Follow alertness, breathing, response and dependence risk.

doseUseReferences.amountText: 192–384 mg base, trying the lower amount first
doseUseReferences.scheduleText: One or two 192 mg capsules orally before bed

substances.name: Meprobamate
substances.summary: Oral anxiolytic with CNS-depressant effects.

indications: Anxiety disorders or short-term anxiety relief.
contraindications: Acute intermittent porphyria or hypersensitivity to meprobamate or related compounds.
majorWarnings: Somnolence, dependence and severe withdrawal may occur. Overdose can cause coma and circulatory collapse.
majorInteractions: Alcohol, opioids and other CNS depressants can intensify depression.
monitoring: Follow alertness, dependence and concurrent medicines. Taper after continued use.

doseUseReferences.scheduleText: Orally in three or four divided doses

substances.name: Tasimelteon
substances.summary: The cited capsules are not directly interchangeable with oral suspension.

indications: Adult non-24-hour sleep-wake disorder.
contraindications: The cited US label lists none.
majorWarnings: Somnolence and impaired alertness can occur.
majorInteractions: Avoid strong CYP1A2 inhibitors and strong CYP3A4 inducers.
monitoring: Follow sleep rhythm and daytime alertness, keeping a consistent daily dosing time.

doseUseReferences.scheduleText: Orally at the same time nightly, one hour before bed, without food

substances.name: Atomoxetine
substances.summary: The cited oral capsules contain atomoxetine hydrochloride with strength expressed as atomoxetine.

indications: Used for ADHD.
contraindications: Hypersensitivity, MAOI coadministration or its washout period, narrow-angle glaucoma, pheochromocytoma or its history, and severe cardiovascular disease that could worsen with higher blood pressure or pulse.
majorWarnings: Monitor for suicidal ideation in children and adolescents. Increased blood pressure or pulse and rare severe liver injury can occur.
majorInteractions: Strong CYP2D6 inhibitors such as fluoxetine or paroxetine can increase exposure. Use caution with pressor drugs.
monitoring: Check blood pressure and pulse before therapy, after dose changes and periodically. Follow mood, pediatric growth and symptoms of liver injury.

eliminationHalfLife.basis: Mean in CYP2D6 extensive metabolizers, about 21.6 hours in poor metabolizers

doseUseReferences.population: Adults, with label-specific titration for strong CYP2D6 inhibitors or poor metabolizers
doseUseReferences.scheduleText: Orally in the morning or split between morning and late afternoon

substances.name: Guanfacine
substances.summary: These details apply to guanfacine extended-release tablets. Immediate- and extended-release tablets differ in exposure and dosing.

indications: The cited US extended-release tablets are used for ADHD alone or alongside stimulants.
contraindications: Hypersensitivity to guanfacine or formulation ingredients.
majorWarnings: Hypotension, bradycardia, syncope and somnolence may occur. Abrupt cessation can cause rebound hypertension.
majorInteractions: CYP3A4 inhibitors and inducers can alter exposure. Sedatives or antihypertensives can intensify related adverse effects.
monitoring: Check blood pressure and pulse before therapy, after dose increases and periodically, and follow sedation. Taper on discontinuation.

tmax.basis: Approximate value after extended-release tablets in children and adolescents with ADHD

doseUseReferences.scheduleText: Orally once in the morning or evening, swallowed whole. Avoid taking with a high-fat meal.

substances.name: Dexmethylphenidate
substances.summary: The d-threo enantiomer of methylphenidate. These details concern immediate-release dexmethylphenidate hydrochloride tablets.

indications: Used for ADHD. The US Focalin tablet dosing information applies to pediatric patients.
contraindications: Hypersensitivity to methylphenidate or formulation ingredients, or concomitant MAOI use or use within 14 days of discontinuation.
majorWarnings: Misuse and addiction are possible. Blood pressure and heart rate can rise, and pediatric growth may be affected. Watch for new psychiatric symptoms.
majorInteractions: MAOIs may precipitate hypertensive crisis. Dexmethylphenidate can reduce the effect of some antihypertensive medicines.
monitoring: Check cardiac and tic history before treatment, and follow blood pressure, pulse, height, weight and psychiatric symptoms.

eliminationHalfLife.basis: Mean terminal elimination about 2.2 hours after oral immediate-release tablets

doseUseReferences.population: Pediatric patients six years or older not taking methylphenidate

substances.name: Viloxazine
substances.summary: The cited US product is viloxazine hydrochloride extended-release capsules.

indications: ADHD in adults and children aged six or older.
contraindications: MAOI combinations or specified washouts, and concomitant sensitive or narrow-therapeutic-range CYP1A2 substrates.
majorWarnings: Watch for suicidal thoughts, increased pulse or blood pressure, somnolence and activation of mania.
majorInteractions: Inhibits CYP1A2. Specified substrates are contraindicated and other medicines require review.
monitoring: Check blood pressure and pulse before and during treatment, and follow mood, sleep and response.

doseUseReferences.scheduleText: Orally once daily, with weekly adjustment per label

substances.name: Pitolisant
substances.summary: Cited tablets contain the hydrochloride salt with strength expressed as pitolisant.

indications: Daytime sleepiness or cataplexy in narcolepsy from age six.

doseUseReferences.amountText: 8.9 mg per day in week one
doseUseReferences.scheduleText: Orally once on awakening, then titrate per label

substances.name: Solriamfetol
substances.summary: Cited tablet strength is expressed as solriamfetol.

contraindications: Concurrent MAOI use or within 14 days of discontinuation.

majorInteractions: Review other pressor or dopaminergic medicines carefully.
monitoring: Control blood pressure before treatment and follow pressure, pulse, wakefulness and psychiatric symptoms, adjusting for renal function.

doseUseReferences.scheduleText: Orally once on awakening

substances.name: Donepezil
substances.summary: The cited oral tablets contain donepezil hydrochloride.

indications: Dementia associated with Alzheimer’s disease.
contraindications: Hypersensitivity to donepezil or piperidine derivatives.
majorWarnings: Nausea, diarrhea, bradycardia or syncope can occur. Watch also for gastrointestinal bleeding and weight loss.

doseUseReferences.scheduleText: Orally once daily in the evening before bed

substances.name: Rivastigmine
substances.summary: Cited capsules contain rivastigmine tartrate with strength expressed as rivastigmine.

contraindications: Related hypersensitivity or prior patch reactions suggesting allergic contact dermatitis without allergy exclusion.

eliminationHalfLife.basis: Approximate plasma value, shorter than enzyme inhibition duration

doseUseReferences.scheduleText: Orally twice daily with meals, titrated to tolerance

substances.name: Naltrexone
substances.summary: The cited oral tablets contain naltrexone hydrochloride. Confirm opioid exposure before initiation.

doseUseReferences.population: Adults screened for opioid-related contraindications per label
doseUseReferences.scheduleText: Orally once daily

substances.name: Acamprosate

substances.name: Varenicline

substances.name: Disulfiram
substances.summary: A sobriety aid that increases acetaldehyde accumulation and causes an adverse reaction to alcohol.

substances.name: Nalmefene
substances.summary: The cited US product is nalmefene injection. Oral tablets for alcohol reduction have separate labeling.

indications: Reverses opioid effects, including postoperative or overdose-related respiratory depression.
contraindications: Product hypersensitivity.
majorWarnings: Can precipitate acute withdrawal and cardiovascular adverse effects. Respiratory depression can recur.
majorInteractions: Antagonizes opioid analgesia and respiratory depression.
monitoring: Secure airway and ventilation, then dose to response. Monitor respiration, blood pressure and withdrawal.

eliminationHalfLife.basis: Mean terminal elimination after IV 1 mg
